content: This includes preventing stigma and discrimination, promoting gender equity, and ensuring that the use of these services remains voluntary. Key populations, who are disproportionately affected by STIs, require increased access to STI services, including treatment for specific infections. This is particularly important for individuals living with HIV and other vulnerable groups. The World Health Organization (WHO) has provided recommendations and guidance in its 2022 Consolidated Guidelines on HIV, viral hepatitis, and STI prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and care for key populations. Additional WHO documents offer further considerations for improving access to and delivery of STI services. Strengthening case-finding efforts for STIs, including HIV and viral hepatitis, and ensuring the availability of laboratory or point-of-care diagnostics are also critical. For trichomoniasis, evidence on the effectiveness of tinidazole, secnidazole, and ornidazole is limited, and randomized controlled trials (RCTs) are needed to compare these treatments with multiple-dose metronidazole regimens. Similarly, for Mycoplasma genitalium, global surveillance is necessary to monitor antimicrobial resistance, and RCTs should evaluate alternative regimens to moxifloxacin and assess sequential therapies. The development of new antimicrobial agents for M. genitalium is also essential. In cases of bacterial vaginosis, further studies are required to compare tinidazole with metronidazole and to explore management approaches for recurrent infections. For anogenital warts, research should assess patient preferences for treatments, quality of life outcomes, and cost-effectiveness. Additional studies are needed for individuals living with HIV and other immunocompromised groups. Health workers should also consider the potential risk of airborne HPV dispersal during ablation procedures. The WHO is committed to disseminating and updating its guidelines through collaboration with regional and national partners, including UN agencies and non-governmental organizations. The guidelines will be shared at relevant conferences and through electronic media, and feedback from end-users will be collected to identify challenges, evaluate their utility, and address gaps in future editions.
